articles.title: Secunderabad Air Force college hit by ₹8.83 lakh vendor fraud
articles.description: HYDERABAD: A New Delhi-based vendor allegedly cheated the College of Aerospace Warfare in Secunderabad of ₹8.83 lakh. The company took advance payments for vegetation clearance work but failed to meet its contractual obligations, as reported by TOI. A wing commander filed a complaint on behalf of the college with the cyber crime police on Thursday […]HYDERABAD: A New Delhi-based vendor allegedly cheated the College of Aerospace Warfare in Secunderabad of ₹8.83 lakh. The company took advance payments for vegetation clearance work but failed to meet its contractual obligations, as reported by TOI. A wing commander filed a complaint on behalf of the college with the cyber crime police on Thursday evening. Police registered a cheating case against unknown offenders under Section 318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Vendor received two advance payments According to the complaint, the college awarded Pinakine Secure Security Solutions a ₹54.8 lakh contract for vegetation clearance through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) on June 5. The Air Force Public Fund transferred two advance payments of ₹4,41,720 each to the company's New Delhi bank account. Officials made the payments on August 19 and September 17 to cover labourers' wages for July and August. Officials could not trace firm's address The complaint alleged that the vendor failed to fulfil its contractual obligations and provided false or non-existent address details. The company also stopped responding to official communications. Officials could not locate the firm's listed address in Hari Nagar, New Delhi. The postal department returned official mail sent to the address, stating that it could not find the company there, according to the complaint. Records identified the proprietor as Sakshi Pandey, but officials could not contact her. Other staff members linked to the firm denied any association with it. They claimed another company had uploaded the tender on behalf of Pinakine Secure Security Solutions. College terminates contract, seeks fund recovery The college terminated the GeM contract after the vendor failed to acknowledge the advance payments despite repeated reminders. The company also stopped responding to official communications. In October, the college filed a complaint on the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal and initiated steps to freeze the firm's bank account. The wing commander has sought police verification of the firm's identity and registration details. The complaint also requests the recovery of the public funds. ]]>
